meetings.title: October 22, 2026 City Council Study Session
meetings.overview: Council received a bike security and theft reduction update showing a 14% year-over-year drop in stolen bikes and a 13% recovery rate, with council raising staffing concerns and suggesting shop and e-bike measures. Council then reviewed the Wildfire Ready 2030 framework, including the WUI Risk Index, Home Hardening Implementation Hub, 14 performance measures, and roughly $1.85 million in proposed 2027 enhancements, and gave feedback to staff, who will return with a progress update in spring 2027. No formal votes were taken.

meetings.title: October 1, 2026 - City of Boulder City Council Regular Meeting with 2027 Budget Public Hearing
meetings.overview: Council heard extensive open comment on CU South, parks, the Boulderthon, cell towers and other issues, then approved the consent agenda and let the Nuropa campus site review proceed without a call-up. After a public hearing on the 2027 recommended budget, council passed budget ordinances 8777 through 8780 on first reading, but a straw poll left wildfire funding changes to be decided at an October 22 study session. Council also straw-polled unanimous support for staff to prepare a resolution backing the Front Range passenger rail sales tax measure.

meetings.title: September 10, 2026 - City of Boulder City Council Study Session (2027 Recommended Budget)
meetings.overview: Council held a study session on the city manager's 2027 recommended budget, totaling $552.6 million across all funds with a $412-417 million operating budget and $135.4 million capital budget, reflecting a second-slowest growth rate since the pandemic and continued reductions. Staff walked through revenue assumptions, goal-area changes, the six-year CIP including wildfire, fire station, and facilities projects, and the long-term financial strategy, then answered council questions on Alpine Balsam oversight, reserves, the auditor function, snow and ice removal, photo enforcement, and possible wildfire funding increases. No formal budget changes were adopted; council members were directed to submit any substantive amendments with identified offsets to the hotline by September 28 ahead of the October 1 first reading.

meetings.title: August 6, 2026 - Boulder City Council Regular Meeting
meetings.overview: The council heard extensive open comment and staff presentations, then voted on five ordinances for the November 3, 2026 ballot. It unanimously referred the firefighter collective bargaining charter amendment (8761), the recreation and safety bond (8758, amended to name a lap pool), and the debt limit charter amendment (8762), and referred the residential vacancy excise tax (8759) by a 7-1 vote. The downtown development authority measure (8763) failed 4-4, and the council then directed staff to scope community engagement; the meeting ended by approving the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan update conditions and amendments.

meetings.title: July 30, 2026 - City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting
meetings.overview: The council held a public hearing on second reading of Ordinance 8754 to amend the local minimum wage code and set a local tip offset amount for food and beverage workers, hearing extensive public testimony from workers, labor groups, restaurant representatives, and residents. After discussion, no motion was made to change the tip offset, so the existing minimum wage schedule will proceed unchanged, and council expressed support for a task force on restaurant sustainability. The meeting also addressed a direction request on a wildfire resilience open space measure, where council agreed to pursue an ordinance rather than a ballot measure and to hold an executive session on legal advice before proceeding.

meetings.overview: The council held a study session covering a Boulder Strong Day of Remembrance declaration, a preliminary look at forming a Downtown Development Authority (DDA) with tax increment financing and a possible November 2026 ballot, and a preliminary discussion of potential 2026 tax ballot measures. meetings.title: February 19, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.overview: The Boulder City Council held its regular Thursday meeting, opening with extensive public comment, mostly from residents urging the city to keep the lap pool at the South Boulder Rec Center. The council unanimously approved the consent agenda and adopted resolution 1370 and ordinance 8734 to annex about 24 acres of city-owned Hogan-Pancost land, along with a land use map change for future parks and flood mitigation. Council also gave non-binding feedback on a concept plan for 281 apartments at 4880 Pearl Street, with members concerned about eroding industrial land.

meetings.title: February 12, 2026 - Boulder City Council Special Meeting
meetings.overview: The special meeting covered a public hearing on whether the Area 3 Planning Reserve warranted further consideration of a service area expansion plan, a city manager matter on reconsidering comprehensive plan community change requests, a municipal court update, and a council community engagement discussion. Council voted 7-2 to find sufficient community need to continue exploring expansion, and directed staff to draft a guardrails resolution for consent agenda adoption at a future meeting.

meetings.title: February 5, 2026 - City Council Regular Meeting
meetings.overview: At its February 5, 2026 regular meeting, council heard extensive public comment, mostly from South Boulder residents urging the city to keep core amenities at the South Boulder Recreation Center, and then unanimously approved the Black History Month declaration and the consent agenda. Council adopted two East Boulder rezoning ordinances for a mixed-use project at 55th and Arapahoe and, after a straw poll, chose to pursue amendments to HB26-1001 (the Home Act) rather than take a flat position. Council also discussed the 2026 policy statement and followed up on its retreat priorities.

meetings.title: January 22, 2026 - City Council Special Meeting
meetings.overview: The Boulder City Council read a Holocaust Remembrance Day declaration, passed a consent agenda unanimously, and unanimously adopted Ordinance 8731, which modernizes city purchasing rules and raises the informal bid threshold to $100,000. The council also approved, with one request removed and two added back, the list of community change requests for the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan update, and directed staff to return with a commercial-focused metro district policy framework for adoption in April. Council closed the meeting after discussing a volunteer for the regional homelessness working group.

meetings.title: January 8, 2026 - Boulder City Council Special Meeting (with Downtown Commercial District, Nwood Metropolitan District, and annexation/ordinance hearings)
meetings.overview: The council heard extensive open comment on Flock Safety cameras, PSPS outages, proportional representation, and other topics, then received a staff recap of the December wind and power shut-off response. It approved the consent agenda including the Sundance Institute governing agreement, approved Downtown Commercial District Resolution 319 for Sundance incentives, and passed the 915 Fifth Street annexation ordinances. It also amended and passed Ordinance 8721 on landscaping, water conservation, and wildfire resilience for a third reading, declined to call up an Arapahoe Avenue form-based code project, and discussed 2026 committee appointments.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Study Session - October 12, 2023
meetings.overview: Council reviewed three items: a Camp (Chautauqua/Shanahan-area) trailhead access management program update, the implementation process for East Boulder subcommunity plan zoning and form-based code, and a discussion of supporting Boulder County ballot measure 1A for open space sales and use tax extension. Council generally supported continuing Camp with planned changes and a feasibility study of direct transit access, asked staff to be cautious about raising fees on residents, and directed staff to refine form-based code review and bring back zoning recommendations; Council unanimously supported measure 1A, with a consent item planned for the next business meeting.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Meeting - Thursday October 5, 2023 (Regular Meeting)
meetings.overview: The council opened with a Indigenous Peoples' Day declaration and National Domestic Violence Month proclamation, then heard extensive open comment on rowing reservoir fees, pollinator gardens, bike path lighting, traffic safety, policing, housing, and budget concerns. It approved the consent agenda including a prairie dog management update and a police oversight ordinance review, annexed a 2.27-acre property at 30333 Street as RL1, and adopted first readings of the 2024 budget with added funding for pavement management, underpass lighting, and community connectors. Council also directed staff to scope a 25-person safe outdoor space pilot.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Study Session - September 28, 2023 (Municipal Court Overview, Police Department Update, and Homelessness Programs Update)
meetings.overview: Council received three presentations: a Municipal Court overview covering its problem-solving approach, Community Court, FastTrack student cases, jail booking constraints and high-utilizer efforts; a Police Department update on rising violent and property crime, fentanyl-driven overdoses, significant incidents and community engagement; and a Housing and Human Services homelessness update on new programs including local vouchers, Building Home, a rest and recuperation center, safe outdoor space options and winter shelter planning. Council members asked for follow-up data and a future conversation on Community Court, and by consensus asked staff to bring a formal item on exploring alternative sheltering, including safe outdoor spaces, with budget implications to be considered.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Regular Meeting - September 21, 2023
meetings.overview: The Council opened with proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month and Energy Efficiency Day, then heard extensive open comment and consent agenda items. The main actions were approving amendments to the Transit Village Area Plan (Boulder Junction Phase 2) and its Comprehensive Plan summary, and amending Ordinance 8599 on zoning for affordable and modest-size housing, with several changes deferred to phase two. The Council also discussed a letter endorsing county housing support, with a directive to bring a formal endorsement back later.

meetings.title: September 14, 2023 - Boulder City Council Study Session
meetings.overview: Council gave staff direction on the intergovernmental agreement with the Boulder Public Library District, including a hybrid trustee appointment process with a three-year check-in and a longer-term lease option with a district-only termination right at five-year intervals. Council then reviewed the $514.8 million recommended 2024 budget, which covers community connector feedback, new investments, capital projects, and unfunded needs. Councilmembers were asked to submit proposed changes by September 25 ahead of the October 5 first reading.

meetings.title: September 7, 2023 - Boulder City Council Regular Meeting
meetings.overview: The Boulder City Council opened with declarations (flood anniversary, National Voter Registration Day, Suicide Prevention Month) and open comment, then approved the consent agenda, including a resolution supporting LGBTQ+ access to public accommodations. The council heard extensive public testimony and accepted the Reimagine Policing Plan and disbanded its subcommittee unanimously. It also received a staff update on inclusionary housing changes, with direction to pursue cash-in-lieu restructuring, reduced on-site requirements, and a possible linkage fee study.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Study Session - August 24, 2023
meetings.overview: The council held a study session covering three items: Community Broadband (staff presented research on three potential paths forward, including a municipal utility, a public-private partnership, and a backbone lease, with council asking for more information on take rates, costs, and lease terms before a future public hearing), the Boulder Airport community conversation (council requested more information on FAA grant obligations and closure feasibility before staff returns in early 2024), and minimum wage (staff reported on regional efforts; council debated accelerating to a 2024 increase, and by a 5-4 split directed staff to stay with the 2025 regional timeline). No formal decisions were made on broadband or the airport.

meetings.title: August 17, 2023 - Regular Boulder City Council Meeting
meetings.overview: The council accepted the clean 2022 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report, heard extensive public comment on minimum wage and other issues, and approved the consent agenda. It placed a 50/50 split of the 0.15 percent sales tax renewal (Ordinance 8591) on the November ballot after defeating the 100 percent arts measure, then adopted Ordinance 8585 to raise the citywide occupancy limit for unrelated persons from three to five after a long public hearing.

meetings.title: August 10, 2023 - Boulder City Council Special Meeting (Board and Commission Appointments) and Study Session (University Hill Revitalization and Affordable Commercial Program)
meetings.overview: The council held a special meeting with a public hearing on 2023 midterm board and commission appointments, then appointed Hannah Davis and Greg Hill, Renee Golbeck and James Lindberg, Harmon Zuckerman, and Tell Jones to vacant seats by acclamation or vote. In the study session, staff presented revitalization strategies for the University Hill commercial area, including district-wide identity, connectivity, and activation efforts, plus a longer-term look at the 14th Street parking lot, and council generally supported prioritizing broad strategies and exploring liquor-rule code changes. Staff also presented a proposed affordable commercial pilot program developed with CU Boulder, and council supported moving forward with its exploration.

meetings.title: August 3, 2023 - Boulder City Council Regular Meeting
meetings.overview: The Council opened with a pollinator appreciation declaration featuring local children, then heard extended open public comment on homelessness, housing, transit, and landmark issues. It passed the consent agenda (with three dissenting votes on the first reading of the occupancy ordinance), designated the Powers House as an individual landmark, and advanced the 50/50 Arts and general fund sales tax compromise ordinance 8591 and the arts petition ordinance 8589 to final reading, while deferring other ballot ordinances to August 17. It also received updates on the 311 Mapleton affordable housing agreement, which now yields a land donation and $1.7 million in cash, and on the homelessness services evaluation and safe outdoor camping planning.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Study Session - July 27, 2023
meetings.overview: The study session covered two items: an update on the police oversight ordinance revision process led by consultant Farah Muscadin, where council discussed ordinance drafting, panel scope, monitor roles, selection criteria, training, and outside counsel, with no formal votes taken. The second item presented Module 3 of the Use Table and Standards update focused on neighborhood centers, including proposals for restaurants, duplexes and townhomes, vehicle-related uses, and other use changes, with council providing direction ahead of a planned October ordinance first reading and November second reading. The meeting ended about 30 minutes early with no formal decisions.

meetings.title: July 20, 2023 - Boulder City Council Regular Meeting
meetings.overview: The Council heard extensive public comment on smoke-free laws, cannabis hospitality, minimum wage, and airport issues. It unanimously passed the consent agenda, including three alternative versions of a sales tax extension ballot measure for first reading. Council took no action to add marijuana hospitality establishments to the work plan or to fund engagement, leaving that question to a future Council, and it then discussed safety on Boulder Creek after recent drownings.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Special Meeting - July 13, 2023
meetings.overview: The council held a special meeting covering a Parks and Recreation Month declaration, a consent agenda, and public hearings on the New Vista High School site development plan and the 4401 Broadway concept plan for a mixed-use creative campus with a new Boulder Museum of Contemporary Art, with no formal approvals taken on those items. In matters from the mayor and council, members discussed unifying competing ballot measures on extending the 0.15 sales tax, and directed staff to prepare a 50/50 alternative split between arts and the general fund, and agreed to defer board and commission vacancies to the 2024 annual recruitment.

meetings.title: June 22, 2023 Boulder City Council Special Meeting and Study Session
meetings.overview: The council amended the agenda, honored retiring Municipal Judge Linda Cook, and approved the consent agenda, including appointing Matt Benjamin and Rachel Friend to the Better Public Meetings project and a 5-2 vote approving the police oversight panel moratorium (Ordinance 8583). It then unanimously adopted Ordinance 8577 rezoning 5405 Spine Road to Business Community. The study session covered a Municipal Court quarterly update, Boulder County Clerk Molly Fitzpatrick's ranked choice voting briefing, polling for a sales tax extension and potential behavioral health tax, and an introduction to the 2024 Boulder energy conservation code.
